html:
The Walangama were an Aboriginal Australian people of inland north Queensland, in the river country southeast of the Gulf of Carpentaria. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Almost nothing is recorded of them beyond their name and the rough bounds of their land. Neighbours on the map include the Mayi Kulan, the Kurtjar and the Takalak. Cattle stations and the gold fields around Croydon in the 1880s brought outsiders into this country. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
